pulls.title: fix CDDL label collision + add grc.basis for result strength
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Two changes, both against the CDDL in Section 4:

1. `grc.room-number` and `grc.hallway-number` both encoded to label 10 — a CBOR decode collision. Moved `room-number` to 13.

2. Adds an optional `grc.basis` (label 14), addressing #2. Rather than a closed list of positioning techniques (which would need extending every time a new one shows up), it reuses the three roles RFC 9334 already defines and this draft already cites normatively: `evidence` (the Attester itself produced the location — a signed GNSS fix, or the proximity measurement in Appendix A), `endorsement` (a third party vouches for it — e.g. a cloud provider's signed statement about a rack), `attestation-result` (a Verifier computed or inferred it — e.g. an operator-selected console region label, which today carries none of the strength of the first two but is indistinguishable from them in the current claims map). An optional `ref` points a Relying Party at the specific supporting claim by digest without embedding it, mirroring how draft-ietf-rats-endorsements keeps Endorsements separate from the Evidence they support.

Verified against a clean build: baseline idnits was 4 errors / 1 flaw / 3 warnings (all pre-existing, unrelated to this section); after this change, identical counts, nothing new introduced. The `&(...)` group-to-choice syntax follows RFC 8610 §2.2.2.2 verbatim.

Happy to adjust the label numbers or field names if you'd rather go a different direction — this is meant to open the specific design question in #2, not settle it.

comments.author: nikolaichuk7
comments.body:
The CDDL on this branch does not parse. With `eat.JC<J,C>` stubbed, using the `cddl` gem 0.12.14:

```
$ cat t.cddl
eat.JC<J, C> = C
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC("corim.uuid-type", 12>

$ cddl t.cddl generate
*** Look for syntax problems around the %%% markers:
grc.claim-uuid = eat.JC%%%("corim.uuid-type", 12>
*** Parse error at 40 upto 40 of 64 (1410).
```

Lines 229 and 230 open the generic argument list with `(` and close it with `>`. Changing `(` to `<` on both fixes it — the `>` is already right. Control: `eat.JC<"corim.uuid-type", 12>` parses and emits `12`.

Fixing the delimiter surfaces two more inside the same five added lines:

```
Duplicate rule definition grm.provence
  -- old: >eat.JC<"grc.provence-values", 13>"]<  (line 230)
  -- new: >tstr .size 8"]<                       (line 233)

Unknown type grc.provence-values
  referenced at line 198, never defined
```

Separately, on the value type. `tstr .size 8` is exactly 8 bytes, so it rejects every form the Provenance Values section mandates:

```
x = tstr .size 8
  "RFC9711"        -> REJECT   (7)
  "RFC123456"      -> REJECT   (9)
  "I-D.something"  -> REJECT   (13)
```

`tstr / uint` accepts all three, and also the bare integer form the section describes.

Rebase note: the base here is `6c12383`, so this branch still carries `grc.hallway-number` and `grc.room-number` both at label 10. On current main `room-number` is 12, and 13 upward are free.

One naming thing, lowest priority: the CDDL spells `provence` while the section heading and registry name spell `Provenance`. The prose is already right.

pulls.title: grm.basis (three artifact classes of RFC 9334) and a label for claim-uuid; two worked examples
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Rewritten after the review of 10 September: one file, no code, no data, no binary files.

- `grm.basis` at label 14: a group-to-choice of the three artifact classes of RFC 9334 Section 4.2 (evidence 0, endorsement 1, attestation-result 2), with prose on what it is and is not.
- `grm.claim-uuid` at label 13 (on main the map key is a bare type name and the definition is misspelled; #9 fixes the names without assigning a label).
- Worked examples appendix: the two public-cloud results (Azure West Europe, basis endorsement, 25 bytes; GCP europe-west4 SEV-SNP, basis attestation-result, 36 bytes), same four jurisdiction bytes, in diagnostic notation with the encoding beside it.

Stacked on #9 (the CDDL name fixes); once #9 merges this diff is the basis change alone. The verifier that produced the examples, with every vector in diagnostic notation, is at https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/geoar-verifier.

pulls.title: (proposal, stacked on #6) basis-ref and an observation window
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Draft, stacked on #6, 41 lines of text, one short example, no code or data. Delete-able as a unit.

**basis-ref (label 16, uuid).** The `claim-uuid` of the result this one rests on. MUST be present when `basis` is `attestation-result` and the consumed result carried a `claim-uuid`; without it the class is a dead end for an auditor. Distinct from `near-to`, which is spatial.

**observed-from / observed-until (labels 17, 18, time).** The interval the observations behind the result cover. A conclusion drawn from a trajectory is about a period, not an instant; the EAR's issue time does not say which period.

Label 15 is left free for the provenance value of #4 (which, as written, uses 13, the label #6 uses for claim-uuid).

The one example is a 57-byte result resting on another result, with the reference and the interval, in diagnostic notation, and a sentence on where it came from. The producer's own data and analysis stay with the producer's document, as suggested; the chain that produced the bytes is at https://github.com/nikolaichuk7/geoar-verifier.

pulls.title: Security Considerations: relayed Results and masked platform identities
pulls.author: nikolaichuk7
pulls.body:
Two short subsections under Security Considerations, as promised on the list (11 September) after Usama Sardar's questions and Giri Mandyam's answer on CHIP_ID.

**Relayed Results.** A geographic Attestation Result states where the Attester's platform was found, not where the Relying Party's peer is; an Attester elsewhere can present a genuine Result obtained by a platform in the attested place (the diversion attack of Sardar, Moustafa and Aura, ASIA CCS 2026, Section 8). The text asks the Relying Party to require that the Evidence behind the Result be bound to the session through a value derived from the session's shared secret (the TLS exporter value of RFC 9266, in the freshness field of the Evidence) and the Verifier to carry that binding into the Result; it says explicitly that binding to a public key alone does not correlate the Evidence with the session, per the binder analysis in ID-Crisis. Measured on 11 September (geoar-verifier, PROTOCOLS.md, protocol 5): through a relay holding the guest's TLS key the key binder accepts and the exporter binder rejects.

**Masked platform identities.** MaskChipId zeroes CHIP_ID in every guest report and VCEK_DIS makes the report key shared across a provider's key domain (SEV-SNP ABI, Rev. 1.58, Sections 3.7, 7.3, 8.18); measured on AWS shared tenancy on 11 September. Per Giri's note on the list, a zeroed identity is an appraisal-policy input, not an error; the text says what it implies for the basis of the Result. Written without reference to the `basis` field so that it applies whether #6 or #4 lands.

References added (informative): ID-Crisis, SNP-ABI, RFC9266. Builds with kramdown-rfc and xml2rfc.

---
Update pushed 11 September (evening), commit 34fdbf0, after Usama Sardar's reply of 19:56Z:

- Relayed Results: the binder analysis is now cited where it lives, Intra-handshake.fail (ESORICS 2026, binding mechanisms 4 and 6), and the text says a public-key binding fails against any other holder of the private key, not only a leaked one; the public key MAY accompany the shared-secret-derived value (its Section 7.2). ID-Crisis stays as the reference for the diversion attack.
- Masked Platform Identities: MaskChipId and VCEK_DIS are independent host choices, neither visible in the report except by its effect; a per-chip signature with a zero CHIP_ID is verifiable only by whoever learns the chip identity from the host side, which makes that certificate an operator statement; the shared key names the provider's fleet without the chip, the per-chip key the chip without the provider (SNP-ABI Section 3.7).
- Measured on 11 September on a bare-metal EPYC Genoa under my control, four launch configurations (geoar-verifier, baremetal/RESULTS.md).
